findings.summary: Garment sprites are back to sleeves drawn as separate bars with a background gap down their whole length. The sweater and the coat are both a shoulder bar with two straight sleeves hanging from it and a gap of about 3 units between each sleeve and the body. At 1x they read as a gate or a table, not as clothing. They also share one silhouette and differ only in the coat's button column, so the two items in one category cannot be told apart by outline. Detached sleeves were one of the regressions this update was meant to fix: published 1.1.0 had them, and rc.6 and rc.7 had fixed them. The rc.8 rewrite of Imagery step 3 brings them back. It says that parts that 'hang free in the real object (sleeves beside a body, two legs, a handle loop) ... keep a 1-unit background gap along the rest of their length', and the agent followed it. Spec-caused, and worse than rc.7. For this item the update goal is not reached.
findings.promptFix: In Imagery step 3 (One silhouette), drop sleeves from the list of free-hanging parts. Write instead: 'A part worn or fixed against the body (sleeve, collar, cuff, strap, lid) touches the body along its whole inner edge, fill against fill, with no background between them. Only a part that really swings free (a handle loop, a hanging tag, a cord) keeps a background gap, and only where the real object shows daylight. Garments are one solid shape: sleeves angle out from the shoulders with the cuff wider than the shoulder joint, never two straight bars parallel to the body.' Add 'a gate or table' to the name test. Also require that set-mates in one category differ in outline (length, width ÷ height, opening, hem) and not only by an inner detail.

findings.summary: Product-card summaries are cut at 2 lines mid-phrase on the catalogue grid at 1440: 'Water-resistant backpack for commutes and short…', 'A two-night bag with a separate shoe…', 'A lightweight knit for layering in every…', 'A sturdy steel mug for coffee at home or…', 'A pre-seasoned pan that works on every heat…', 'A simple loop of vegetable-tanned…'. Published 1.1.0 shows them whole in 3 lines in the same 5-column cards, and rc.7 had fixed this. rc.8 is built on rc.6, whose Card rule still says 'at 2 lines in .tiles and product cards', so the regression comes back. Spec-caused, and worse than published.
findings.promptFix: In Card → Anatomy, change the description rule to: 'whole in .cards (clamped past 4 lines); in item cards whole up to 3 lines, clamped only past 3; 2 lines only in .tiles; a clamp never cuts a summary that would fit in one more line.'

findings.summary: The store detail banners are one per category, not one per item: 4 banners for 11 products. The agent says a unique scene for each product was not practical (commerce agent-report.md, Decisions). This goes against Pixel stage step 1 ('every ... detail or content page has its own lead sprite'). The reference does the same thing, though: one banner per category, shared by the category page and its articles (reference p7-i1.png and p4-i1.png show the same snowy Infra banner). So it is fidelity rather than a defect, and the spec is stricter than its source. The two captured detail pages are in different categories and show different leads.

Empty-state titles render at body size ('No posts match these filters', 'No projects match your filters'), so the title barely outranks the hint line under the vignette. The same watch item was raised on rc.7. It now appears in both apps that have an empty result.

Two more catalogue sprites fail the name test at 1x. The key ring is a flat brown bar with a hole, which reads as a strap or a USB stick: no key, and nothing hangs from it. It is no longer a magnifier, so it is still better than published. The tea towels read as two cans or a thermos.

The settings strips use small slab and cross shapes (a teal rounded slab, a dark arched slab, upright crosses or signposts). At 1x they read as headstones and grave crosses, giving the 'civic street' strips a graveyard feel. On the Profile strip the moon is also cut in half by the right edge of the window.
The dashboard user menu opens with no option highlighted or marked, and no ▶ on 'Account settings'. The spec asks dropdowns to open with the first or current option focused and highlighted.

In the Security 'Change password' window at 1440 the three fields are about 560px wide in a window about 1000px wide, which leaves a band about 400px wide empty to their right. The Profile form fills its window in two columns, so the two settings windows look inconsistent.

notes: SCOPE (screen step, 1 sample). Run folders: showcase/runs/night-cartridge/1.2.0-rc.8/<app>/20261018-103529/. Published = 1.1.0-rc.2/<app>/20261015-034853/. Earlier verdict = 1.2.0-rc.7/critic-1.json, which had no blockers or majors, only watch items E (cart void) and F (empty-state title size). Every gate passes in all four apps (eval-1.md). Palette consistency 0.875, type consistency 1. The harness measured no layout defects, so there was nothing to confirm or dismiss. Every finding is '1 of 1'. Not penalized (known harness gaps): the sticky header captured mid-page in full-page state shots (commerce state-checkout-errors and state-added-to-cart, dashboard state-empty-filter, blog state-search-empty, settings state-profile-errors-mobile); the dialog scrim ending at about 900px (settings state-plan-dialog-desktop-dark.png); leftover temporary review files that agents could not delete (all four agent-report.md).

UPDATE GOAL (1.2.0, leftovers from the 1.1.0 review). Hero lead identity: REACHED. A printing house with a gear plate and a real 'INK' sign, sawtooth roof and chimney, plus a moon, clouds and a diagonal stepped path (blog/drawings/home-d1.png). Product-page sprite: REACHED. The tote is about 273 of 602px, about 45% (products-canvas-field-tote-desktop-light.png). Newsletter title: REACHED ('Subscribe to the newsletter' h2). Store name on mobile: REACHED ('Fieldhouse Supply' in full, commerce home-mobile-light.png). Mobile table: REACHED (Project and Status only, dashboard home-mobile-light.png). Hero hill: the teal rim and stepped slope separate it from the ground. Mobile hero: the lead shows whole under a thin band of sky (blog home-mobile-light.png). The band is thinner than in rc.7, where the lead was smaller; low confidence from the scaled capture, not scored. Sweater sleeves: NOT REACHED. The rc.8 Imagery rule brings the gap back (major finding 1).

RC.8'S OWN GOALS. (3) Controls sharing a row at one height: REACHED in every app checked. Blog email + Subscribe, settings Save changes + Reset, dashboard search + Search, and commerce stepper + Remove all line up. (1)/(2) Generalization: the four agents built their own worlds from the general rule: a printers' street, a supply yard, a container port and a civic street. No demo world leaked from the spec. But the generalized garment rule caused finding 1, and building on rc.6 instead of rc.7 dropped rc.7's product-card summary fix (finding 2).

COMPARED WITH PUBLISHED 1.1.0. Better: the tote (two separate handle loops, rim and pocket, wider than tall; published read as a padlock), the key ring (no longer a magnifier), the hero lead, varied blog banner leads (INK press house, NEWS kiosk, library; about 105–120px tall), the cart layout (summary stacked under Items, so rc.7's watch item E no longer applies), and same-height controls. Equal: sweater and coat. Published had detached sleeves too, so the update goal is missed there, though not worse than published. Worse: product-card summaries clamped at 2 lines (finding 2).

SIGNATURE (3). Present in all four apps and placed as Applying the concept says. Blog: a full-bleed hero with a framed title window, banners with their own lead per article and about, an inline figure, vignettes. Store: grid and cart strips, a banner per category on detail pages. Dashboard and settings: a strip per screen. Every screen has the checkered ground strip. Motion is stepped: blog motion-m1.png shows nc-drift at 120000ms with steps(60), and motion-m3.png shows nc-swap at 500ms with steps(1). Sprites are 41–47% of their grid windows. Why 3 and not 4: the garment sprites regress (finding 1). Also, as in rc.6 and rc.7, the strip props are 20–50px and simpler than the reference's snow-laden trees and figure at the same scale (reference/illustrations/p2-i2.png vs dashboard/drawings/home-d1.png).

OTHER SCORES. Reference fidelity (4): night ground, cream pixel type, 4px windows, dither rules under h2s, one gold commit with a hard shadow, the gold ▶ marker, hue top bars and bullets, block meters and the grass strip, as in reference/screenshots/p1-desktop-light.png and p1-i1.png, without copying the cabin, figure or snow. Cross-app consistency (4): one family. Blog and store use top navigation, dashboard and settings a sidebar, with the same windows, chips, meters and strip. Hierarchy (4): scene and h1 first, 48px KPIs, a 48px price with the gold Add to cart; weakened by the clamped summaries and the body-size empty-state titles. Spacing (4): the 4px scale holds and dashboard panels end level; the password form band is minor. Component states (4): card hover shows the marker and a raised card (commerce state-card-hover-desktop-dark.png). Invalid fields get a gold focus frame on the first one, danger frames and '!' messages (commerce state-checkout-errors-desktop-dark.png). The plan change opens a titled dialog with a framed close button, Cancel and a gold Confirm (settings state-plan-dialog-desktop-dark.png). Loading shows skeleton KPI tiles and a disabled 'Refreshing ...' button. Empty results show a vignette, a 0-of-n meter and a framed ▶ Clear filters. Polish (4): radius 0, 2/4px borders, no leftover browser defaults.

VERDICT INPUT. No blocker. Two majors, both spec-caused and in the only sample, so both count against the prompt: the garment sleeve gap prescribed by the new Imagery step 3 (also a miss of the update goal and a regression from rc.7), and the 2-line product-card clamp (worse than published). The minors are listed once and are not reasons to fail.
